name: DWG FastView Plus
tagline: Desktop viewer positioned as an alternative light client for plotting and reviewing DWGs on Windows.
meta_desc: Often used when full authoring is unnecessary but fidelity and speed matter for QA. Verify download source (vendor-linked CadWonder endpoints) and version against your DWG baseline.

terms.title: Fidelity QA Viewer
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Fidelity QA Viewer inside DWG FastView Plus.
terms.definition: Fidelity QA Viewer opens drawings with high accuracy, letting users check layers and measure dimensions.
terms.why_matters: Provides a safe QA review environment without risks of accidental geometry modifications.
common_pitfalls: Failing to verify scale settings before taking layout measurements
Using outdated viewer versions that do not support recent DWG formats

quiz.question: When working with Fidelity QA Viewer, which of the following represents a common technical pitfall?
options: Failing to verify scale settings before taking layout measurements.
Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Failing to verify scale settings before taking layout measurements.' As the editorial review notes: 'Provides a safe QA review environment without risks of accidental geometry modifications.'

terms.title: Batch Plotting Utility
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Batch Plotting Utility inside DWG FastView Plus.
terms.definition: Batch Plotting Utility publishes batches of DWG files to PDF or print formats simultaneously.
terms.why_matters: Saves release coordination time and enforces consistent plot scaling across drawings.
common_pitfalls: Applying incorrect CTB plot styles to batch lists causing thin lines
Publishing layouts with unlocked viewports, causing scale shifts

Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Applying incorrect CTB plot styles to batch lists causing thin lines.' As the editorial review notes: 'Saves release coordination time and enforces consistent plot scaling across drawings.'

terms.title: Markup Layer Merge
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Markup Layer Merge inside DWG FastView Plus.
terms.definition: Markup Layer Merge aggregates markup entries from multiple reviewers into a unified sheet database.
terms.why_matters: Simplifies change management and provides a clean record of requested revisions.
common_pitfalls: Merging conflicting markups without resolving discrepancy first
Orphaning annotations by changing the underlying base drawing coordinates

faqs.question: What are the advantages of FastView Plus over standard FastView?
faqs.answer: FastView Plus is a high-performance Windows desktop application designed to handle extremely large DWG assemblies and run batch plotting and audit diagnostics.

faqs.question: How do I configure batch printing with specific plot styles?
faqs.answer: Open the Batch Plot utility, select multiple drawings, load your enterprise `.ctb` file, select target printer/PDF generator, and run.

faqs.question: Can I merge markups from different team members in FastView Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes. FastView Plus can load multiple markup layers on top of a single base drawing, allowing you to merge annotations into a master revision list.
